PullRequest.Title: chat: add participant and tool-set migration guidance

## Summary

Add guidance-only customization migrations for third-party extension chat participants and explicit user-defined or extension-contributed tool sets. Neither has an automatic migration, so the customization modal shows read-only entries with **Learn More** links:

- https://aka.ms/vscode-migrate-customizations/chat-participants
- https://aka.ms/vscode-migrate-customizations/tool-sets

Guidance contributes to migration notices and counts and supports existing Ignore/Restore behavior. It stays separate from executable candidates, with no selection, row actions, automatic migration, or inclusion in Migrate with Agent. A guidance-only dashboard explains that automatic migration is unavailable.

Excludes core/default/dynamic and built-in Copilot participants, synthetic extension tool groups, and internal/MCP/external tool sets. Includes deprecated user tool sets. Updates accessibility content, tests, and themed fixtures.

No linked issue was provided.

## Validation

- `npm.cmd run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `node --input-type=module -e "import { runBuildFast } from './build/next/build-fast.ts'; await runBuildFast(process.cwd(), false, true);"` — client build passed; pre-publication check confirmed inputs and outputs remain up to date. Direct entry invocation avoids the local Node version's unsupported `import.meta.main` guard.
- `npm.cmd run test-browser-no-install -- --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\aiCustomization\customizationMigrationServiceImpl.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\aiCustomization\aiCustomizationManagementEditor.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\aiCustomization\customizationMigrationDashboard.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\aiCustomization\chatCustomizationMigrationNotice.test.ts --browser chromium --reporter dot` — **132 passed**.
- Changed-file ESLint: `$files = git --no-pager diff --name-only -- '*.ts'; & .\node_modules\.bin\eslint.cmd --cache --cache-strategy content --max-warnings 0 $files` — passed before commit.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Component Explorer — **11 render/disposal checks passed**. Reviewed mixed dark, narrow guidance-only light, and high-contrast screenshots; repeated captures matched.

Electron/native dependency setup was unavailable, so unit tests ran in Chromium. Live extension discovery has not been validated end to end.

## How to review

Use the `MigrationsGuidance` and `MigrationsGuidanceOnly` fixtures under `chat/aiCustomizations/customizationMigrationDashboard`. Verify that MCP retains its migration controls while participant/tool-set groups have only Learn More and Ignore. The guidance-only view must not offer Migrate with Agent. Tests cover discovery filtering, mixed/guidance-only counts, documentation URL activation without navigating the workbench, and Ignore/Restore.

Requested reviewers: @hawkticehurst and @aeschli.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed subscriptions, excluded item classes, event firing sites, downstream consumers, and filesystem/MCP call paths are all directly traced. Exact timing and cache warmth vary, which limits severity, but the unfiltered fan-out and cold-path boundary work are deterministic.
Findings.PerformanceResource: filesystem searches and reads, extension-provider discovery calls, secret-storage checks, and repeated migration-plan allocations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost grows with the number of agent/tool-set registration events times the number of live migration consumers and, on each discovery, with configured prompt locations, workspace folders, and distinct MCP source files. Agent registration commonly fires again for implementation/metadata updates, and MCP/internal tool sets also change even though both classes are excluded from guidance.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: excessive I/O and repeated/cancelled discovery work during extension activation and MCP/tool initialization, increasing startup and migration-surface latency
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Agent implementation/metadata changes and language-model tool-set changes were not part of onDidChangeCustomizations, so chat notices, Sessions navigation, and other subscribers did not rerun full migration discovery for those events.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added Event.map(onDidChangeAgents) and toolSets observable are broadcast directly through onDidChangeCustomizations. Consumers respond by calling computeMigrationHint or refreshing the editor; computeMigrationHint runs all migration categories in parallel, including four unique prompt-file inventories and MCP migration planning.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT lines 64-65 add chatAgentService.onDidChangeAgents and the entire toolsService.toolSets observable to the shared invalidation event, without filtering to the participant/tool-set inventory accepted by RIGHT lines 83-104 or coalescing bursts.
Findings.Title: Filter guidance changes before invalidating all migration discovery
Findings.Impact: When extensions or MCP servers register participants/tool sets, every live migration notice/navigation/editor consumer can restart full discovery. Cold or invalidated prompt caches search user/workspace locations and extension providers, while MCP planning reads each distinct source configuration and may query secret storage; bursts cancel prior work without globally coalescing the replacement calls.
Findings.Evidence: ChatAgentService.onDidChangeAgents fires for registerAgent, registerAgentImplementation, updateAgent, dynamic agents, and disposal, although computeMigration filters core/default/dynamic participants. ILanguageModelToolsService.toolSets contains internal and MCP sets, although computeMigration accepts only user and eligible extension sets; MCP tool sets are created per enabled server. ChatCustomizationMigrationNotice and CustomizationsNavigationState subscribe to onDidChangeCustomizations and immediately call computeMigrationHint. That method invokes UserData, PromptFiles, ConfiguredLocations, and MCP discovery; listPromptFiles cold paths scan user/local locations and extension providers, and AgentHostMcpServerMigrationProvider.createPlan reads grouped MCP source files. These newly irrelevant events therefore fan out into concrete boundary work.
Findings.Recommendation: Expose a guidance-inventory change signal that fingerprints only eligible static third-party participants and user/eligible extension tool sets, and fire once when that filtered inventory actually changes. Ignore implementation/metadata-only agent events and internal/MCP/external/hidden tool-set churn; coalesce registration batches before forwarding to full migration consumers.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench or Sessions window startup / extension activation while migration availability consumers are live
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Agent or tool-set registration fires the shared customization event; chat migration notices and Sessions navigation synchronously schedule computeMigrationHint, whose result gates notice/navigation availability. Prompt inventory and MCP planning must settle before availability updates.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover prompt/agent/instruction/skill files across user and local configured locations
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four effective prompt types per hint; each cold type scans user and local sources/configured locations. Calls are shared by per-type promises when warm/in-flight, but cancellation can clear a cold promise.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These scans already occurred for real migration invalidations, but agent implementation/metadata and generic tool-set registrations did not newly trigger them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks each hint computation and thus migration-notice/navigation availability.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke extension-contributed prompt providers while collecting each prompt type
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one provider inventory per contributing extension and prompt type on a cold/invalidated cache, coalesced by the same per-type promise.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Provider discovery was not triggered by agent/tool-set registration events solely due to those events.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read MCP source configuration and inspect secret storage while constructing the migration plan
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One source-file read per distinct eligible MCP source URI per hint, plus secret checks for OAuth-bearing configurations; independent hint consumers are not globally coalesced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The boundary existed for migration discovery, but irrelevant participant/tool-set churn did not add these hint computations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks MCP category and therefore the aggregate hint.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of agent lifecycle and tool-set events multiplied by live consumers; cold work further scales with four prompt types, configured source locations/workspace folders, extension providers, and distinct MCP source files.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each computeMigrationHint runs categories with Promise.all. Prompt reads can share per-type cached promises, but separate notice/navigation/editor consumers independently run aggregate discovery and MCP planning. Successive observable events cancel a consumer's prior autorun store rather than coalescing the burst globally.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm prompt inventories return cached promises/arrays, reducing this to allocations and MCP planning; file-change invalidation or startup is cold. Cancellation of the token that created an in-flight cached prompt promise causes it to reject and clear, so registration bursts can restart cold discovery. No cache/coalescer covers aggregate hints or MCP plans.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the new unfiltered event sources, excluded inventory classes, downstream immediate recomputation, and cold boundary paths are directly established.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact overlap between registration bursts and live UI consumers, plus cache warmth and number of MCP sources, varies by window and extension set.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium regression: irrelevant/excluded inventory churn now fans out full migration discovery without filtering or batch coalescing.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open Chat Customizations migration editor and dashboard refresh
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The editor's zero-delay Delayer coalesces synchronous notifications, then computes all enabled executable categories and both guidance inventories before updating the dashboard; target-folder provider calls follow discovered candidate types.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Prompt inventory discovery for enabled executable categories
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One compute per enabled category after Delayer coalescing; underlying repeated prompt types share prompt-service caches.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The editor refreshed for direct prompt/MCP events; this diff additionally connects it to the broad shared event.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query harness item provider for destination source folders
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per distinct target prompt type after candidate deduplication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same calls occurred on editor refresh before the diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Enabled migration categories, candidate files, participant/tool-set counts, and distinct target types.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Categories and two guidance enumerations run concurrently; destination-folder calls then run concurrently by distinct target type. Delayer(0) coalesces same-turn editor events and cancellation discards stale results, but it does not coalesce with notice/navigation consumers.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Guidance inventories are uncached in-memory snapshots and inexpensive; prompt inventories use per-type caches. MCP planning and provider target-folder queries are recomputed.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Editor-open frequency and provider cost vary; the broader unfiltered shared event is the meaningful added cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: Covered by the reported shared-invalidation finding; no separate editor-only finding because its Delayer bounds synchronous duplicate notifications.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render and interact with guidance-only or mixed migration dashboard
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Stored guidance arrays are mapped to tree entries and DOM rows synchronously during overview rendering. Learn More crosses the opener boundary only after explicit user activation and is not on render/startup critical paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the fixed Learn More URL via IOpenerService
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one opener call per user click/keyboard activation; no prefetch or automatic request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The guidance action did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only affects the explicitly requested navigation, not dashboard rendering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of eligible third-party participants and explicit user/extension tool sets, typically small and bounded by installed contributions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Rendering is synchronous and proportional to visible guidance items; opener calls are user-paced with no background burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No relevant cache; current guidance snapshots are retained only by the editor lifecycle and replaced on refresh.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large extension inventories could increase row allocation, but no realistic unbounded or hot-loop mechanism was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: proportional DOM work is required to display the inventory, and the only introduced boundary is explicit, one-per-click navigation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Compute migration hints after a legitimate prompt, MCP, participant, or eligible tool-set inventory change
Scenarios.CriticalPath: All executable migration categories and the two new in-memory inventories complete before the hint count/message is returned.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing prompt and MCP migration discovery
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four effective prompt inventories and one MCP plan per hint; guidance adds two in-memory O(n) enumerations but no boundary calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Executable discovery already ran; participant/tool-set counts were absent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks the hint as before; guidance enumeration adds only local array/filter/map work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Eligible participant and tool-set counts for added local work; existing prompt locations and MCP sources dominate boundaries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Seven categories execute with Promise.all; participant/tool-set inventory reads are synchronous and do not increase external concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Prompt results are cached per type; participant/tool-set snapshots are recomputed from current services and not retained by the migration service.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Inventory sizes vary but are normally small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding for adding the inventories themselves; their local O(n) cost is appropriate. The issue is only the unfiltered event frequency reported above.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 13 changed files. One medium missing-coalescing/boundary-fanout regression was submitted for broadcasting every agent and tool-set lifecycle change into full migration discovery, including excluded inventory classes. Guidance enumeration, dashboard rendering, retention, and explicit Learn More navigation did not establish additional regressions.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
